text:
Evan Brooks: Heads-up - ProofPoint wants an RFI row that explains POC rollover behavior if Dedicated underprovisions. They specifically asked for escalation steps, costs, and a short legal-safe one-liner.

Sana Iqbal: Suggest 'POC Rollover & Escalation' row. Steps: 1) auto-burst to hosted-variant (if enabled), 2) notify customer + open support incident, 3) offer temporary Dedicated scale-up quote, 4) optional contract amendment for capacity.

Tom Reyes: They care about operation during rollover: expected p99 hitting ~320ms on hosted variant for mid-size seq. Add a conservative note: "During rollover, latency may degrade up to 50% vs dedicated baseline."

Evan Brooks: Procurement wants a single-cell worst-case monthly delta for budget. CostEstimator, can you produce a rough number for 30 qps chat POC, baseline Dedicated reserved, with 12 hours/day rollover to hosted for 7 days?

CostEstimator: Baseline (Dedicated 2x mid-gpu reserve): $16,200/mo. Scenario: 12h/day to hosted for 7 days (30 qps, avg 220 tokens/session) => additional hosted charges ~ $4,600. Worst-case monthly delta (that window): +28% (~$4.6k). Provide cell: 'Worst-case (7d, 12h/day overflow): +$4.6k (+28%)'.

Sana Iqbal: For security, they asked about data flow during rollover. security-bot, can you confirm short wording for RFI?

security-bot: RFI text suggestion: "When controlled rollover to hosted occurs, request payloads transit encrypted (TLS 1.3) and processing occurs in Redwood-managed regions; customers requiring no egress can disable rollover by policy. Audit events for rollover actions are logged and exportable."

Tom Reyes: Add a tiny cell about cache warm behavior: "Cold cutover may incur ~30-120s rewarm; long-context sessions may see up to 3m to reach steady-state."

Evan Brooks: Legal asked for a single-line procurement-safe clause about liability. Sana, any draft?

Sana Iqbal: Draft: "Controlled rollover may be enabled by mutual agreement; Redwood is not liable for cross-region transfer where the Customer has expressly authorized rollover in writing."

Tom Reyes: Also include an example CLI/API snippet for the 'initiate-rollover' call in the appendix so their infra team can test. Short example below.

Tom Reyes: ```bash
# initiate controlled rollover for project 'proofpoint-poc'
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/projects/proofpoint-poc/rollover \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"mode":"controlled","target":"hosted-variant-lowlatency","drain_seconds":300}'
```

Evan Brooks: Nice. Procurement also wants a clear table cell that says whether rollover requires a signed addendum. Answer?

Sana Iqbal: Yes - default: rollover is opt-in and requires Controlled Rollover Addendum to be signed for accounts with data residency flags. Put in RFI cell: 'Requires addendum if data-residency flag set'.

CostEstimator: Quick note: include a line that hosted egress and cross-region fees are billed separately and can materially affect worst-case numbers.

Evan Brooks: Great. I'll insert rows: Feature: 'Controlled Rollover', Default: 'Disabled (opt-in)', Exit: 'Customer API/console trigger + drain', Audit: 'Logs retained 540d (exportable)', Cost typical: '+15-25% on overflow', Cost worst-case: '+$4.6k (7d scenario)'. Then send draft to ProofPoint.

security-bot: Reminder: include link to redacted network diagram and SOC excerpt in attachments. Suggest links: https://files.redwood.internal/sales/proofpoint/network_redacted.png and https://files.redwood.internal/sales/proofpoint/soc_excerpt.pdf

Evan Brooks: Perfect. I'll attach those and get legal to bless the one-liner. Targeting EOD send. :thumbsup:
